etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English gile, from Anglo-Norman gile, from Old French guile (“deception”), from Frankish *wīl (“ruse”), from Proto-Germanic *wīlą, from Proto-Indo-European *wey- (“to turn, bend”). Cognate via Proto-Germanic with wile.
senses: (uncountable) Astuteness often marked by a certain sense of cunning or artful deception.
